messages:
Elliot: @Aisha quick question — Priya on my team just disclosed shes been having panic attacks and PTSD symptoms triggered by nighttime pager alerts. Shes asking to be removed from weekend on-call temporarily while she gets treatment. Can People Ops advise on what we need (docs, timeline) and whether we can reassign weekend coverage without it affecting her upcoming performance review?

Aisha: Thanks for flagging and for keeping this confidential, Elliot. We can start the ADA/interactive process. At a high level: employee sends a request (email is fine) + any supporting documentation (doctor note or short letter). We can approve a temporary job modification (e.g., no weekend on-call) while we evaluate — typical temporary windows are 30–90 days and can be extended. Well coordinate with you on operational coverage so theres no gap. HR will treat docs as confidential and store them in the private HR file.

Priya: Hi — yes, Im comfortable sharing a note from my provider. Weekends are the worst for me. Id prefer to be on weekdays only if possible. Also worried about how this will show up in the performance cycle — Im already nervous about the review.

Aisha: Totally understandable. We will notate this as a temporary accommodation and it should not be used as a negative in the review. Please email the docs to accommodations@redwood.com or reply here if you want me to set up a private intake call. Once we have the request and documentation we usually respond with an interim decision within 3–7 business days. If you need immediate relief, we can put a provisional adjustment in place the same day while paperwork is pending.

Sam: I can take Priyas weekend slots for the next two rotations. Quick rotation swap idea:```week1: Sam, week2: Alex, week3: Sam, week4: backup-plan```Ill update the rotation calendar and ping the team. No problem covering weekends for a bit.

Elliot: Thanks Sam — can you add the calendar invites and update the pager runbook to show Sam as primary for weekends? Also Ill document the accommodation plan in Priyas one-on-one notes and make sure its reflected in our manager comments for the cycle.

Priya: Thanks all — that helps a lot. Ill send the provider note to accommodations@redwood.com now. Appreciate the quick coverage offer, Sam.

hr-bot: Accommodation request received. Ticket #ACM-2026 created. HR will follow up. If you need immediate assistance, contact people-ops on-call.

Aisha: Quick next steps for Elliot: 1) keep the request confidential (do not share docs outside HR), 2) implement temporary coverage (Sams change) and avoid assigning alternative duties that reintroduce weekend alerts, 3) document expectations for Priya during the accommodation period (e.g., core hours, deliverables), and 4) check in weekly with Priya and HR for at least the first month. I can draft a short manager note you can reuse.

Elliot: Will do. Please DM me the draft manager note, Aisha — Ill send it to Priya and update her one-on-one agenda.

Priya: One more ask — can we keep the accommodation window open for renewal? Im not sure how long this will take.

Aisha: Yes — accommodations can be extended. After the initial 30/60/90-day period well revisit with Priya and the manager. If treatment progress is slower, we can renew. If anything changes (workloads, symptoms), let HR know and well reconvene. Also reminder: EAP counseling is available and fully confidential — see https://internal.redwood/hr/eap for details.

Elliot: Thanks team. Ill implement the rotation change and keep weekly check-ins. :thumbsup:

Priya: Thank you. Really appreciate the quick support.

Aisha: Thanks everyone. Closing loop once accommodation ticket is resolved (hr will post an update in the ticket).
